Meridian Elementary School had 5 multiracial students in 2024-25
Meridian Elementary School enrolled five multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year, a 37.5% decrease from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Records show Meridian Elementary School had 313 students in the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students made up 1.6% of the enrollment, the second least represented group. White students were the largest group, accounting for 87.2% (273) of the student body.
The school is part of Grosse Ile Township Schools District, which has its central office in Grosse Ile.
Across the district's four schools, Grosse Ile Middle School had the largest multiracial student enrollment in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which declined by just 2 points.
Achievement gaps among ethnic groups also persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students. The gap was wider for Black students, who scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
